classification.difficultyReason: Identify equal-area regions, count the shaded fraction, and convert it to a percentage; the triangular partitions require recognising eighths.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts identify a shaded fraction of one square and convert it to a percentage; percent-meaning is the closest directly assessed skill.
questions.methodNote: Page 2 models percentages using equal parts of a hundred-square. Page 6 defines percentages and converts fractions to percentages by multiplying by 100%. Page 8 Example 8 applies the part-over-whole calculation.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Count equal shaded regions and express their fraction of the whole as a percentage.

classification.difficultyReason: Write each percentage over 100, simplify, and express improper fractions as mixed numbers using the taught conversion.

questions.mappingNote: Every part directly converts a percentage to a fraction; parts g–l also require the mixed-number representation used in the source teaching.
questions.methodNote: Write the percentage over 100 and simplify. Page 2 demonstrates 65% and 150%; page 6 Example 3a, b demonstrates 45% and 135%, using mixed numbers for values above one. Page 8 Example 8 provides surrounding percentage context.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply the displayed percentage-to-fraction method, simplifying and expressing values above one as mixed numbers.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert percentages to decimals directly through equivalent fractions with denominator 100, including percentages above 100 and below 10.

questions.mappingNote: All twelve parts directly assess the demonstrated percentage-to-decimal conversion, including values greater than 100% and single-digit percentages. No supplied reuse candidate matches this complete task.
questions.methodNote: Page 2 establishes percentages as parts per hundred. Page 6 states that a percentage is first written as a fraction with denominator 100 and then converted to a decimal; Example 3c and d demonstrate this for 45% and 135%. Page 8 supplies the exercise and its Example 3c, d margin reference.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert percentages to decimals directly through equivalent fractions with denominator 100, including percentages above 100 and below 10.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert fractions with denominators 10, 100 and 1000 directly to percentages.

questions.mappingNote: Every part assesses fraction-to-percentage conversion. Parts a–f use the direct per-100 interpretation, g–l equivalent hundredths, and m–t the exact denominator-1000 method of Example 4. The supplied reuse candidates have different complete tasks and are not source-equivalent.
questions.methodNote: Page 3 converts fractions to equivalent fractions with denominator 100 and also teaches multiplication by 100%. Example 4 on page 6 reads a denominator-100 fraction directly as a percentage and converts a denominator-1000 fraction by multiplying by 100%, simplifying to tenths of a percent, then writing a decimal. Pages 2, 4 and 7 support percentage meaning and fraction conversion.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert fractions with denominators 10, 100 and 1000 directly to percentages.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply multiplication by 100%, converting mixed numbers first where needed; all parts follow the demonstrated conversion procedure.

questions.mappingNote: Every part assesses fraction-to-percentage conversion. Parts g, i and n additionally require the mixed-number conversion demonstrated in Example 5c. Parts h, m and o give exact terminating decimal percentages; no rounding is required.
questions.methodNote: Page 3 establishes multiplication by 100%. The summary on page 6 repeats that rule. Example 5 on page 7 multiplies fractions by 100%, simplifies common factors and converts mixed numbers to improper fractions before multiplying. Page 4 supplies common equivalents; page 2 establishes the meaning of percentages.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert proper, improper and mixed fractions to percentages, including decimal percentages.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct conversion of terminating decimals to percentages by multiplying by 100%.

questions.mappingNote: Every part directly assesses decimal-to-percentage conversion, including decimals greater than one and decimals with hundredths. No rounding is required.
questions.methodNote: PDF page 3 teaches decimal-to-percentage conversion by multiplying by 100%, with 0.6 = 60% and 3.2 = 320%; the summary on PDF page 6 repeats this rule. Pages 2, 4 and 7 support equivalent representations.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct conversion of terminating decimals to percentages by multiplying by 100%.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert mixed fractional percentages to simplified fractions using equivalent fractions.

questions.mappingNote: Every part directly assesses conversion of a mixed fractional percentage to a simplified fraction. Neither supplied reuse candidate is the same original task.
questions.methodNote: Write the percentage over 100, multiply numerator and denominator by the denominator of its fractional component, then simplify. Page 2 demonstrates halves and thirds; Example 6 on page 7 demonstrates quarters. Pages 4 and 6 reinforce equivalent fractions and percentage conversion.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert mixed fractional percentages to simplified fractions using equivalent fractions.

classification.difficultyReason: Select the appropriate taught conversion from each given representation, using place value, fraction simplification and percentage scaling to fill the labelled columns.

questions.mappingNote: All twelve table rows assess conversion between fractions, decimals and percentages; no percentage-of-quantity calculation is required.
questions.methodNote: Pages 2–3 establish percentages as fractions with denominator 100, simplification, decimal conversion and multiplication by 100%. Page 4 supplies common equivalents. Examples 3–6 on pages 6–7 model the same conversions, including values greater than one.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Complete equivalent decimal, fraction and percentage forms using familiar conversions, including thousandths and values greater than one.

classification.difficultyReason: Forms a part-to-total fraction and converts it to a percentage; part b first requires common units.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts directly assess expressing one quantity as a percentage of another. The supplied chapter evidence demonstrates the percentage method, but does not establish prerequisite metre/kilometre teaching for part b.
questions.methodNote: Page 5 Example 2 and page 8 Example 8 express the selected quantity over the total and multiply by 100%. Pages 3 and 7 support exact fraction-to-percentage conversion, including mixed fractional percentages. Use common units before forming a ratio.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Forms a part-to-total fraction and converts it to a percentage; part b first requires common units.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct percentage calculations using familiar fraction equivalents, including mixed-number percentages.

questions.mappingNote: Every part directly finds a percentage of a stated quantity. Familiar fraction equivalents make the mixed-number percentages exact; percentage-of-quantity is the most advanced directly assessed skill.
questions.methodNote: Page 4 supplies all fraction equivalents used here. Page 5 Example 1 and page 7 Example 7 demonstrate converting a percentage to a fraction, simplifying, and multiplying by the quantity. Page 3 supports percentage conversion; page 8 distinguishes expressing one quantity as a percentage of another.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct percentage calculations using familiar fraction equivalents, including mixed-number percentages.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert the stated percentage to a multiplier and apply it to the supplied quantity; percentages above 100% use the same direct method.

questions.mappingNote: All twelve parts directly calculate a percentage of a supplied quantity. No reuse candidate matches this complete question.
questions.methodNote: Page 7, Example 7, writes the percentage as a fraction over 100, multiplies by the quantity, simplifies and evaluates. Pages 4–5 introduce this method through Example 1. Page 3 establishes conversion from percentages; page 8 establishes the Exercise 7A context.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct percentage calculations, including percentages above 100% and decimal results.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct percentage calculations with whole-number and simple fractional percentages.

questions.mappingNote: Every part directly calculates a stated percentage of 340. Parts e and f additionally convert a mixed-number percentage to a fraction; percentage-of-quantity is the most advanced directly assessed skill.
questions.methodNote: Page 5, Example 1, and page 7, Example 7, calculate a percentage of a quantity by multiplying the quantity by the percentage written as a fraction over 100 and simplifying. Page 7, Example 6, demonstrates converting a mixed-number percentage to a fraction. Pages 3–4 support percentage conversions; page 8 concerns expressing one quantity as a percentage of another.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct percentage calculations with whole-number and simple fractional percentages.

classification.difficultyReason: Directly calculates familiar percentages of a whole-number quantity.

questions.mappingNote: All three parts directly assess finding a percentage of a quantity using the demonstrated fraction method.
questions.methodNote: Page 4 gives 25% = 1/4, 75% = 3/4 and 12 1/2% = 1/8. Page 5 Example 1 and page 7 Example 7 calculate a percentage of a quantity by writing the percentage over 100, simplifying and multiplying.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Directly calculates familiar percentages of a whole-number quantity.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct calculations of 10%, 30% and 5% of stated whole-number quantities.

questions.mappingNote: All four parts directly assess finding a percentage of a given quantity. Each part retains its own numerical givens and uses the demonstrated fraction-multiplication method.
questions.methodNote: Page 3 explains percentages as fractions with denominator 100. Pages 4–5 introduce and demonstrate finding a percentage of a quantity. Page 7, Example 7, multiplies the percentage fraction by the given quantity and simplifies before evaluating. Page 8 demonstrates the reverse comparison task, which is not required here.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct calculations of 10%, 30% and 5% of stated whole-number quantities.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct percentage calculations using the explicitly required fraction method.

questions.mappingNote: All three parts directly assess finding a percentage of a quantity, with fraction conversion and fraction multiplication explicitly required.
questions.methodNote: Page 4 gives common fraction–percentage equivalents. Page 5, Example 1, expresses the percentage as a fraction over 100 and multiplies by the quantity written over 1. Page 7, Example 7, simplifies the fraction before multiplication. These methods give 9.6 m, 60 lollies and 81 children.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct percentage calculations using the explicitly required fraction method.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct percentage calculations with the decimal method explicitly specified.

questions.mappingNote: All three parts directly assess finding a percentage of a quantity. Decimal multiplication is an explicitly required supporting method.
questions.methodNote: Page 3 converts percentages to decimals by dividing by 100. Pages 4–5 introduce finding a percentage of a quantity; page 7 Example 7 demonstrates multiplication using percentage fractions. Question 16 explicitly requires decimal multiplication, so its solutions convert each percentage to a decimal and multiply by the quantity. The supplied teaching pages do not demonstrate the prerequisite decimal-multiplication algorithm.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct percentage calculations with the decimal method explicitly specified.

classification.difficultyReason: Expresses two monetary amounts in the same unit as a percentage using a direct ratio.

questions.mappingNote: The task directly assesses expressing one monetary quantity as a percentage of another. Both amounts already use dollars, so no unit conversion is needed.
questions.methodNote: Page 5, Example 2, and page 8, Example 8, express the selected quantity over the total and multiply by 100%. Page 3 explains conversion of fractions to percentages.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Expresses two monetary amounts in the same unit as a percentage using a direct ratio.

classification.difficultyReason: Directly expresses one monetary quantity as a percentage of another in the same units.

questions.mappingNote: Both monetary amounts use dollars, so their ratio directly assesses expressing one quantity as a percentage of another.
questions.methodNote: Page 5, Example 2, and page 8, Example 8, express the required quantity over the comparison quantity and multiply by 100%. Page 3 supports converting fractions to percentages.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Directly expresses one monetary quantity as a percentage of another in the same units.

classification.difficultyReason: First infer Carla’s stamp count, then express it as a percentage of Mike’s count.

questions.mappingNote: The assessed task expresses one quantity as a percentage of another, with one preliminary subtraction.
questions.methodNote: Page 8, Example 8, divides the relevant quantity by the comparison whole and multiplies by 100%. Page 3 explains fraction-to-percentage conversion; page 4 supplies familiar fraction-percentage equivalents. First subtract 27 from 72 to obtain Carla’s count, then use Mike’s 72 stamps as the comparison whole.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: First infer Carla’s stamp count, then express it as a percentage of Mike’s count.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert fractions to exact percentages containing mixed fractional parts.

questions.mappingNote: Each of the six parts directly assesses fraction-to-percentage conversion using the method of Example 9. The visible Example 9 margin reference is retained as editable text. Neither supplied reuse candidate is identical to this complete six-part task.
questions.methodNote: Page 3 establishes multiplication by 100%; Example 9 on page 11 converts a fraction to an exact mixed fractional percentage. Pages 12–13 extend this method to quantities. Retain exact fractional percentages without rounding.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert fractions to exact percentages containing mixed fractional parts.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert mixed-number percentages to fractions by clearing the fractional numerator and simplifying.

questions.mappingNote: All twelve parts directly assess conversion of mixed-number percentages to fractions. Each follows the denominator-clearing method of Example 10, retaining exact arithmetic.
questions.methodNote: Page 11, Example 10, writes a mixed-number percentage over 100, multiplies numerator and denominator by the fractional denominator, and simplifies. Page 3 establishes percentage conversion; pages 12–13 concern the reverse conversion of ratios to percentages and do not replace Example 10's method.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert mixed-number percentages to fractions by clearing the fractional numerator and simplifying.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert whole, decimal and mixed-number percentages to simplified fractions.

questions.mappingNote: Every part directly assesses percentage-to-fraction conversion. Decimal percentages require clearing the decimal numerator; part f uses the mixed-number numerator method explicitly demonstrated on page 11.
questions.methodNote: Use percentage as a fraction with denominator 100. Clear decimal or mixed-number numerators by multiplying numerator and denominator by the same factor, then simplify, following page 11's changing-percentages-to-fractions demonstration and Example 10. Pages 12–13 concern the converse quantity-to-percentage method.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert whole, decimal and mixed-number percentages to simplified fractions.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert decimal and greater-than-100 percentages to decimals and simplified fractions.

questions.mappingNote: Every part directly assesses percentage-to-decimal-to-fraction conversion. Parts a–e require simplifying decimal fractions; parts f–h exceed 100% and retain exact mixed-number answers matching the teacher key. The supplied reuse candidates do not contain this complete task.
questions.methodNote: Page 3 converts percentages to decimals by division by 100. Page 11 converts percentages to fractions and simplifies them, including mixed-number results in the broader conversion context. Pages 12–13 concern quantities expressed as percentages; their ratio equality chains are not needed here. Write the decimal first, express that decimal as a fraction using place value, then simplify exactly.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert decimal and greater-than-100 percentages to decimals and simplified fractions.

classification.difficultyReason: Use the explicitly specified order to form first-number-over-second-number, multiply by 100%, and simplify to an exact percentage.

questions.mappingNote: Each of the six pairs asks for the first number as a percentage of the second, directly assessing quantity-as-fraction-percentage. The offered reuse candidates are not identical whole tasks: neither contains this shared instruction and these six pairs.
questions.methodNote: Example 11 forms first quantity divided by second quantity, multiplies by 100%, simplifies and retains an exact mixed fractional percentage. Pages 3 and 11 establish fraction-to-percentage conversion; Example 13 continues the quantity comparison method. Authored working starts with the complete percentage calculation to avoid equating a ratio directly with its numerical percentage coefficient.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Express one quantity as a percentage of another, including exact mixed fractional percentages.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert three scores with different totals to exact percentages and rank their relative performance.

questions.mappingNote: The main assessed skill is expressing each score as a percentage of its test total. Comparing those percentages supplies the requested ranking. Each multiplication expression is retained on the left of its working chain to avoid an incorrect equality between a ratio and its numerical percentage coefficient.
questions.methodNote: Express each score as score divided by total, multiply by 100%, and simplify exactly. Page 12 Examples 11–12 demonstrate fractional percentages and comparison of quantities with different wholes; page 11 Example 9 retains exact mixed fractional percentages.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert three scores with different totals to exact percentages and rank their relative performance.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the state population as the whole, calculate the capital's percentage, then use its complement for the population outside.

questions.mappingNote: Both parts assess population proportions expressed as percentages; part b uses the complementary portion of the same whole.
questions.methodNote: Express the relevant quantity over the whole and multiply by 100%, as demonstrated in Example 2 on page 5 and Examples 11–12 on page 12. The whole population represents 100%, so subtract the capital-city percentage to obtain the outside percentage.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Express a population subset as a percentage of the whole, then find the complementary percentage.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the relevant part and whole in context and convert their ratio to an exact fractional percentage.

questions.mappingNote: The 1250 rollercoaster riders are the part and the 3200 park entrants are the whole; finding their percentage directly assesses quantity-as-fraction-percentage.
questions.methodNote: Express the part as a fraction of the whole, multiply by 100%, simplify and retain the exact mixed-number percentage, as demonstrated in Example 11 on PDF page 12.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the relevant part and whole in context and convert their ratio to an exact fractional percentage.

classification.difficultyReason: Find the number who died from the survivor count, then express it as a percentage of all infected people.

questions.mappingNote: The required quantity is the number who died, so subtract the 15 survivors from the 300 infected people before forming the fraction.
questions.methodNote: Express the required quantity as a fraction of the whole and multiply by 100%, as demonstrated by the swimming-club example on PDF page 5.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find the number who died from the survivor count, then express it as a percentage of all infected people.

classification.difficultyReason: Calculate an expected number from a percentage, then convert a recovery fraction to a percentage to compare two drugs.

questions.mappingNote: Part a assesses percentage of a quantity. Part b assesses expressing one quantity as a percentage of another and comparing effectiveness; this supplies the primary skill.
questions.methodNote: Find a percentage of a quantity by multiplying by the percentage written over 100, as in page 5 and Example 7 on page 7. Express recoveries as a percentage using recovered divided by treated, multiplied by 100%, then compare percentages, as in Example 12 on page 12.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate an expected number from a percentage, then convert a recovery fraction to a percentage to compare two drugs.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert to exact percentages and subtract, retaining fractional percentage differences.

questions.mappingNote: Question 11 assesses conversion followed by the difference between percentage representations. The Exercise 7B answer key confirms subtraction rather than relative percentage increase.
questions.methodNote: Convert fractions and decimals to percentages by multiplying by 100%; retain exact mixed-number percentages, then compare by subtraction.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert to exact percentages and subtract, retaining fractional percentage differences.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert two differently expressed proportions to percentages and compare three close values.

questions.mappingNote: The assessed result is an ordering of three proportions expressed as a fraction, a part-to-whole count and a percentage; ordering fractions, decimals and percentages is the primary skill.
questions.methodNote: Multiply a fraction or part-to-whole ratio by 100% and compare the resulting percentages. Page 11 Example 9 gives the exact conversion of 2/7 to 28 4/7%; page 12 Example 12 compares proportions by converting them to percentages.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert two differently expressed proportions to percentages and compare three close values.

classification.difficultyReason: Students determine the common total before expressing four quantities as percentages, retaining exact fractional percentages.

questions.mappingNote: The whole is the total number of loaves sold. Each bread-type count is expressed as a percentage of that total, directly assessing quantity-as-fraction-percentage.
questions.methodNote: Express each quantity as a fraction of the whole and multiply by 100%. Retain exact mixed-number percentages where the decimal recurs, following Examples 9, 11 and 12.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Students determine the common total before expressing four quantities as percentages, retaining exact fractional percentages.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the relevant part and whole in each situation, recognise that the population units already match, and convert each ratio to a percentage.

questions.mappingNote: Both parts directly assess expressing one quantity as a percentage of another. Part a uses matching million units; part b uses the original 32 pieces as the whole.
questions.methodNote: Express the part as a fraction of the whole and multiply by 100%; retain exact fractional percentages where appropriate, as in Example 11 on PDF page 12.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the part and whole in each situation and convert their ratio to an exact percentage.

classification.difficultyReason: Choose the supplied percentage corresponding to each person's gender and multiply it by their mass, reporting kilograms.

questions.mappingNote: Both parts directly assess finding a percentage of a given mass; the gender determines which supplied percentage applies.
questions.methodNote: Write the percentage as a fraction with denominator 100 and multiply by the quantity, following Example 1's supplied working on page 5.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Select the stated percentage for each person and calculate that percentage of their mass.

classification.difficultyReason: Add three percentages, then express the total as a simplified fraction.

questions.mappingNote: Each part directly assesses conversion of an added percentage total to a fraction, so convert-fractions-decimals-percentages is the closest catalogue skill.
questions.methodNote: Page 15 demonstrates adding percentages. Page 2 teaches writing a percentage over 100 and simplifying, multiplying numerator and denominator when necessary to obtain whole numbers. Page 7 reinforces fraction conversion; pages 16–17 distinguish addition from multiplication.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Add three percentages, then express the total as a simplified fraction.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert both percentages to fractions, multiply, and convert back to a percentage using the explicitly taught method, retaining exact fractional values.

questions.mappingNote: Every part directly calculates a percentage of another percentage; percentage-of-quantity is the closest catalogue skill. Fraction conversion and multiplication support the assessed method.
questions.methodNote: Example 17 on page 17 converts both percentages to fractions, simplifies, multiplies and converts the product back to a percentage. Pages 2 and 7 support exact conversion of fractional percentages.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find products of percentages, including fractional percentages, using exact fraction arithmetic.

classification.difficultyReason: Two direct products of percentages using the method demonstrated in Example 17.

questions.mappingNote: Both parts directly assess finding a percentage of a quantity, with the quantity itself expressed as a percentage; fraction–percentage conversion supports the calculation.
questions.methodNote: Example 17 on PDF page 17 converts each percentage to a fraction over 100, simplifies and multiplies the fractions, then expresses the result as a percentage.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Two direct products of percentages using the method demonstrated in Example 17.

classification.difficultyReason: Calculate 65% of the stated group for the count and subtract 65% from 100% for the complementary percentage.

questions.mappingNote: Part a directly assesses a percentage of a quantity; part b applies the whole-group meaning of 100% and the complementary-percentage method.
questions.methodNote: Example 7 on PDF page 7 calculates a percentage of a quantity by multiplying its fraction over 100 by the quantity. Example 15 on PDF page 16 subtracts a known percentage from 100% to find the complementary group.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate a stated percentage of a whole and subtract the percentage from 100%.

questions.methodNote: Example 7 on PDF page 7 converts a percentage to a fraction over 100 and multiplies by the quantity. PDF page 15 permits addition for non-overlapping groups of the same whole; Example 15 on PDF page 16 subtracts their total from 100% to find the complement.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate three percentages of a common whole, then use complementary non-overlapping groups to find the remaining number.

classification.difficultyReason: Calculate two percentage quantities and use the complement of two non-overlapping groups.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a and b directly assess percentages of 500. Part c combines the same-whole, non-overlapping percentages and calculates the remaining quantity; percentage-of-quantity is the closest catalogue skill for the complete task.
questions.methodNote: Example 7 converts a percentage to a fraction over 100 and multiplies by the quantity. Pages 15–16 permit addition of percentages of the same whole for non-overlapping groups and subtract their total from 100% to find the complement.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Calculate two percentage quantities and use the complement of two non-overlapping groups.

classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that 6% refers only to the male subgroup, then multiply the nested proportions to express that subgroup relative to the whole herd.

questions.mappingNote: Question 7 has the same subgroup-within-a-whole structure as Example 18: 6% of the male subgroup, which comprises 15% of the whole herd.
questions.methodNote: Convert percentages to fractions with denominator 100, multiply and simplify, then convert the resulting fraction to a percentage, as demonstrated in Examples 17 and 18 on PDF page 17.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Interpret a percentage of a subgroup and multiply percentages to express the result relative to the whole herd.

classification.difficultyReason: Distinguishes a complement of the whole from a percentage of a subgroup.
